response.query: Which ELBO estimator choices (single vs multi-sample S, control variates) and reparameterizations minimize gradient variance for diag-Gaussian posterior with CAR/GP priors?

We provide an overview of key techniques, including the variational inference method for posterior approximation, the Gaussian process as a regression surrogate, Bayesian quadrature, Variational Bayesian Monte Carlo (Acerbi 2018")), and sparse Gaussian processes. Variational inference is a popular approach to approximate the intractable posterior density \(p(\textbf{x}|\mathcal {D})\) via a simpler distribution \(q(\textbf{x})\equiv q\_{\varvec{\phi }}(\textbf{x})\) that belongs to a parametric family indexed by \(\varvec{\phi }\) (Jordan et al. When a computational model of interest has an expensive black-box likelihood, a proven approach for efficient Bayesian inference consists of building a (cheaper) *surrogate model* to emulate either the log-likelihood \(\log p(\mathcal {D}| \textbf{x})\) or directly the log joint density function \(f\_0(\textbf{x})\); see Figure 1. results.content: Haoyue Tang · Tian Xie · Aosong Feng · Hanyu Wang · Chenyang Zhang · Yang Bai. Solving image inverse problems (e.g., super-resolution and inpainting) requires generating a high fidelity image that matches the given input (the low-resolution image or the masked image).By using the input image as guidance, we can leverage a pretrained diffusion generative model to solve a wide range of image inverse tasks without task specific model fine-tuning.To precisely estimate the guidance score function of the input image, we propose Diffusion Policy Gradient (DPG), a tractable computation method by viewing the intermediate noisy images as policies and the target image as the states selected by the policy.Experiments show that our method is robust to both Gaussian and Poisson noise degradation on multiple linear and non-linear inverse tasks, resulting into a higher image restoration quality on FFHQ, ImageNet and LSUN datasets.
